title: Summary​
content: A brief summary is conveniently located at the top of the default selected Overview Tab which gives you an idea of how your project is doing at a general scope. The two leftmost lists outline some fields that were assigned when creating the project (and can be edited in the Project Settings Window). We also list the number of activities in the latest schedule and some other key parts of the project that you can find on various other components/tabs of Metius. The right ride of the component tracks the following metrics: Contract ∆: days between the current completion, and contract completion datesDriving Critical Activity: The incomplete critical activity that is driving critical workQC Issue: The potential schedule issue category with the greatest impact to the project's QC scoreFloat Consumption: The % difference in average float compared to the previous updateProgress Performance: The progress only impact to the schedule compared to the previous updateCritical Path Reliability: The overall score from the Critical Path Reliability component found on the Risk tab

title: Overview Components​
content: This tab is meant to be a summary, so we hand-picked some of the most critical and informative parts from all the components on the project detail page to catch you up with the project's progress as fast as possible. Seeing something that looks amiss on this page is a good indication that you should dig deeper on other tabs of the project page for the sake of your project. Here is a list of the components we included on this page, as well as any information that makes them unique on this tab: Progress Trending: Just the current period bullet charts from the full Progress Trending ComponentProject Completion Trending: This one was so important, we included the whole chart from the Progress TabCritical Path: The same chart as on the full component; we just set the views to be critical activities only and in the 90 day lookahead timespanActivity Completion: The 90 day lookahead planned view from the Activity Completion Compnent. This one still has the intractability of the left side activity type filter boxes to show a task listQuality Control Review: This component is just the Potential Schedule Issues subset of the entire Quality Control Review Component. Similarly to that component, select an issue type to view the activities contained. This component is replaced with the DCMA Component if your project settings' Quality Calculation Method is set to DCMA

title: Gantt Overview​
content: The Reports Page features Gantt data for all activities from the most recent update. On the table to the left there are a variety of important columns that can be configured in the Column Selector. To the right there are gantt bars that greatly helps visualize the timeline of your project's activities. The red line going through the gantt timeline shows the Data Date of the most recent update.

title: Filter Menu​
content: This button opens a window that allows you to apply multiple layered filters to your project. Add multiple filters within filter groups to really nail down the specific activities you are looking for. These filter options are also included as part of the Report Form, where we go over an example of the filters in action.

title: Group By​
content: An individual window that can be used to apply groupings to your project's activities by either activity codes or wbs. Further description and images are in the Report Form

title: Choose Columns​
content: Column selector for fields visible in the gantt chart's left pane. It is also available as an option in the Report Form.

title: Report Center​
content: The Report Center is the hub to manage your report templates and batch-export to PDF multiple reports or even entire folders. The buttons at the bottom of the window allow you to: create new folders (personalized collection of reports)create new reports (templates used to display different activities/relationships in the gantt chart)quick save (save currently displayed gantt layout as a new report template)Add multiple reports to a folder (Requires report checkbox selection)export to pdf (batch export all selected reports to your email after a few minutes. Requires report checkbox selection)

title: Report Window​
content: The Reports window combines all transformation options for the gantt chart into one window to be used as a form. You can press the apply button to see your changes first before saving your report or save the report to add it to this project's Report Center. If you got to this window through an edit icon click, clicking save will update that report's values instead. The general options require a name for the report for your own identifying purposes (reports are tied to projects, so everyone with access to the project can see the report name). Additionally, there are options to base this report on previously created reports (functions like the duplicate button) and 2 management options: Add to Favorites and Add to Folder. These two are more for organizational purposes to either make this report show up in the Favorites Menu or inside a specific folder in the Report Center respectively. Relationships Toggle​ Simple toggle to show/hide the relationships arrows on the gantt bars with the default being hide. Criticality Toggle​ Simple criticality toggle with options to display all activities or only critical activities with critical being the default. Visible Columns​ The same column selector as seen here. By default, the first 7 columns will be checked and visible. All columns, except for the activity ID, can be unchecked to hide or checked to display. Filters​  A 'Gantt Filters' window will appear when this button is clicked that can help narrow down your chart to see the activities you desire. You can add as many groups which consist of as many filters as needed. The buttons 'And' or 'Or' can be selected for each group which will allow you to create powerful and specific filters to match your ambitions. info For this example from the above screenshot, the filtered activities that would show up after hitting apply will be activities that either have an ID equal to 'SUB-1170' OR have a status equal to 'Complete' AND an activity name equal to 'Project Complete'. As you can see, utilizing groups and changing the and/or logic lets you create filters that can showcase complex subsets of activities, allowing you to quickly make visual aids for meetings and presentations. Grouping​ You can group activities by WBS or by Activity Codes, so you can easily view all your tasks in the format you prefer. Simply select either 'WBS' or 'Activity Codes' to enable your desired grouping method. You may collapse or expand any of these sections to help visualize how each group is performing. The grouping row is distinctive by its dropdown icon and highlighted color. You can view aggregate values for all activities within the group such as overall start and finish dates for the entire group, or the total remaining duration. We provide a default color scheme for easier visibility to differentiate grouping levels but you can easily customize these colors for you project by clicking on the color and selecting a new one in the grouping section. Grouping by WBS​  This feature allows you to group your project's activities based on their WBS Codes. Select the maximum depth level you want the grouping to go through, or press the 'All' button to select all levels. We included the WBS tree (accessible through the button on the top left of Options) where you can collapse/expand and see exactly what each level includes to aid your grouping decision. Grouping by Activity Codes​  This feature allows you to group your projects activities based on their Activity Codes. You may select multiple activity codes by clicking the arrow buttons to add Activity codes to the 'Group By' section. Use the up and down arrows within the 'Group By' section to reorder the grouping levels as needed. The above screenshot showcases adjustments to the grouping level colors.

title: Favorite Reports​
content: When clicked, the Favorite Reports button will open a small menu displaying all favorite reports and a few buttons. These buttons redirect you to the report center (maybe to adjust which reports are your favorites), add a new report, quick-save a new report with the current gantt settings, and close the menu. You can also quickly edit/duplicate/delete favorite reports with the icons in the report list. danger Deleting a report completely removes all traces of it from this project permanently. If you meant to just remove a report from your favorites list, you can do so by opening the report center and clicking the star next to the desired report.

title: Collapse/Expand One Level​
content: These two buttons are only enabled when a WBS or Activity code grouping is applied. These buttons make it easy to collapse or expand one grouping level at a time. The expand or collapse button will be disabled if you have fully expanded or collapsed all possible levels respectively.

title: PDF Export​
content: Download the current gantt display into a PDF. Additionally, the pdf will display the project name, update name, and update date on the top of your pdf image.

title: Project Score​
content: The Project Score is the overall score, and is calculated as an average of three sub-scores: Progress Score, QC Score, and Risk Score. Note that the Risk Score is not factored in the baseline schedule project score.

title: Progress Score​
content: The Progress Tab houses the components that contribute to the Progress score which, like the name implies, is a measure of the progress of your project as of the current update. Some key contributors to this score are the Float Consumption component (specifically the Baseline Variance and Previous Update Variance) and the Activity Completion Ratios which are weighed by criticality. The Progress Score is composed of three sub-values: Component	WeightActivity Completion Index	70% Period Float Index	20% Baseline Float Index	10%

title: Activity Completion Index​
content: The Activity Completion Index measures how well scheduled activities in the previous update meet their deadlines. It is calculated as the percentage of start and finish dates scheduled to occur by the next actual data date that actually did occur. Note that the start and finish estimates for the same activity are counted and checked individually. If the activity is a non-finish milestone, it will use the early start for both start and finish checks. The Activity Completion Index is weighted according to the criticality of the activity the dates belong to. Component	WeightCritical	50% Near Critical	40% Non Critical	10%

title: Float Index​
content: The Float Index scores the difference in activity float distribution by percentage between two updates. Component	Penalty per 1% increase	Max PenaltyNegative Float	0.5%	40% No Float	0.5%	40% Week Float	1%	10% Month Float	1%	7% Large Float	1%	3%

title: QC Score​
content: The QC Score focuses on the quality of the schedule. The maximum QC score is 100%, and points are deducted for potential schedule issues, which are located on the Quality Tab. For the default QC Score Calculation Method, points are deducted from this score for: High Duration Task or Resource Activities with Remaining Duration >= 44 Days High Float Activities with Total Float > 80 + Critical Float Days Start-to-Start/Finish-to-Finish (SS/FF) with problematic lags SS Relationships with lags become problematic when the lag duration > remaining duration of the incomplete predecessor OR when the lag duration > original duration of complete predecessorFF Relationships with lags become problematic when the lag duration > remaining duration of the predecessor Open Start/Finish Open Start - an activity’s only predecessors are FF relationshipsOpen Finish – an activity’s only successors are SS relationshipsIf an activity has any FF or FS relationship in addition to the SS successor relationship, it is not an open condition Missing Predecessors or Successors Predecessors/successors must be non-LOENo deduction for start/finish milestones Negative Lags May affect logic/critical path Finish-to-Start (FS) with Lags May overstate risk in the schedule Hard Constraints Mandatory Start or Mandatory FinishOverrules logic/scheduled dates, incompatible with Monte Carlo simulations Out of Sequence Incomplete activities that have started before the predecessor has completed Logic Density 2 x Relationships / Activities Start-to-Finish (SF) Relationships Should the QC Score Calculation Method be set to DCMA, the score is based on the amount of tests passed out of the amount of tests available for this update/project (tests can be deselected in the Quality Tab in Project Settings)

title: Risk Score​
content: The Risk Tab encompasses the components that play a part in determining the Risk Score. This score utilizes forward-looking components to give a warning of potential risks in the remainder of your project. For the baseline, the Risk Score will be the average of: Average of CPLI and BEICritical Path ReliabilityMonte Carlo Score (if available) If the Monte Carlo Score is not available for later updates, it will be the average of: Average of CPLI and BEICritical Path RiskCritical Path Reliability Otherwise, it will have the weighted score: Component	WeightMonte Carlo Score	50% Critical Path Risk	20% Critical Path Reliability	20% Average of CPLI and BEI	10% CPLI (Critical Path Length + Total Float) / Critical Path LengthIf the finish activity has a constraint date and early finish, the total float will be the difference between the two datesCPLI < 1 indicates that the schedule is progressing inefficiently with regard to the completion date BEI Percentage of baseline activities projected to be complete that actually completedBEI < 1 indicates that the activities are not completing as planned in the baseline schedule Critical Path Reliability Critical Path Reliability measures the consistency of the activities on the critical path and logic ties between them. The overall score is an average of the sub-scores:Activity Consistency - gauges if activities remain critical, with a zero indicating a total path change and 100 indicating an identical path between the schedules, after correcting for completed activities (Maintained Previous Critical Activities ^ 2) x 100 / ((Previous Critical Activities - Completed Previous Critical Activities) * Critical Activities) Previous Logic / Update Logic - measures changes in the driving logic ties along the critical path of both the n - 2 schedule to the n - 1 and the n - 1 to the current update. These two values are averaged for an overall Logic Consistency score Previous Logic: (Previous Driving Ties - (Deleted Driving Ties + Previous Lag Changes)) / Previous Driving TiesUpdate Logic: (Current Driving Ties - (Added Driving Ties + Current Lag Changes)) / Current Driving Ties Critical Path Risk Day Difference In Path	Deduction Per Day	Max DeductionPrimary Path	1.5%	50% Secondary Path	1%	30% Tertiary Path	0.75%	20%Analyzes the critical, and sub-critical paths to provide stability information and trends Low Risk = 85% to 100%Moderate Risk = 50% to 84%High Risk = 0% to 49% Monte Carlo Score The % of progress between the data date and current completion vs between the data date and the P85 dateComputed as 1 - (calendar days between current completion and P85 date) / (2 x calendar days between the current completion and data date) and if the Risk Calculation Method chosen for your project is any of the Monte-Carlo methods, then the Monte-Carlo on-time probability joins the four aforementioned components in determining the Risk Score.
